correctness.rationale: For C=K=I in H=ell2(N), F=(e_j) is Parseval. G=(e_2,e_2,e_3,...) has all nonzero unit atoms, but (T_F-T_G)c=c_1(e_1-e_2) has rank one while T_G*e_1=0. Thus G cannot have a strictly positive lower frame bound. Theorem 3.7 of Rajput--Sahu--Mishra as actually printed only demands compact E=T_F-T_G and range/commutation conditions, all automatic with C=K=I and T_F onto. The optional bound ||E||<sqrt(A) implies (sqrt(A)-||E||)^2 lower bound by reverse triangle inequality, explicitly Hilbert-space only. The failure is infinite-dimensional and exact, not extrapolated from numerics.
